title: Germany's far-right AfD emerges as landslide winner in eastern state vote

article.title: Germany's far-right AfD emerges as landslide winner in eastern state vote
article.summary: Germany’s far-right AfD won a landslide victory in a key regional election Sunday in the ex-communist east, taking at least 44 per cent of the vote according to exit polls by two public broadcasters. “We have made history today,” said a jubilant Ulrich Siegmund, the 35-year-old lead candidate of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in Saxony-Anhalt state. It was, however, too early to tell whether the AfD will have enough votes for an absolute majority that would allow it to govern a state alone for the first time. The centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz came a distant second, winning around 18.5pc, according to exit polls by broadcasters ARD and ZDF . Depending on the eventual count, the CDU’s state premier Sven Schulze would hope to still be able to form a new multi-party coalition to block the AfD from power. All major parties have so far maintained a “firewall” of non-cooperation with the Moscow-friendly AfD, whose state branch is categorised as “right-wing extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence agency.
